lines: Behind the Race door, Map Select now draws the whole unlock path.
It reads Maps: each map opens the next. A new rider starts with two open, Prairie Paceline and Old Town Criterium.
The backend serves the seven maps from a catalogue file, in unlock order, and anyone can read it before signing in.
An open map links to Race Setup, with its photo, distance, climbing and rating, and its stars. A best time shows once it's ridden.
The next unlock is ringed in gold, with its facts and its goal: finish top three against bots on Prairie Paceline.
Every other locked map is greyed, with a lock, and names its one goal: a race, a star count, or a rider level.
Colour is never the only sign. A screen reader hears locked, or locked, your next unlock.
Beside the path, stars on every map: finish, top three against the medium pack, and beat your best.
Once read, the catalogue stays on the device. With none kept and no network, Map Select says so, and Try again asks again.
The same path, from a phone to a desktop, where the star rules sit beside it.
What the tests prove: seven behaviour specs and the backend's catalogue tests, all green, and the first bundle still under budget.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
